analyst_view.overall: Early view: Girona, relegated from LaLiga last season, have lost two in a row 1-0 but still have the most attacking quality in the division (Vanat, Asprilla, Stuani, Carles Pérez). Eibar are fourth and play with less of the ball than anyone, per one report; their postponed game at Castellón still has to be rescheduled and could add a midweek fixture before this one.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.3 goals. I lean higher: Girona's home games have included a 5-1 against Celta Fortuna and a 2-0 against Andorra, and Eibar's last three away league games had two, four and four goals. Girona's finishing should recover after Vanat hit the post against Almería.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.2 corners. I lean higher: Eibar concede possession by design, so Girona should spend long spells in their half, and Girona's wide players (Carles Pérez, Asprilla) give them the crossing and shooting that earn corners.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.7 cards. Girona collected three first-half yellows against Almería and Jokin Aranbarri wants an aggressive Eibar, but Girona usually control home games, so I hold at the site's figure.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.7 shots, with 18.1 for Girona, which fits a home side facing a team that gives up the ball. Girona's recent shot counts were low (eight with ten men, 12 against Almería), but Eibar's style should give them more room, so I keep it.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target. Girona's quality should turn volume into accuracy, but Eibar's deep defending forces efforts from distance, so I see no clear lean.
